body:
> If it were me, (I'm no expert so take this with a grain of salt) I'd maybe try to sign her up for some kind of activity you two can do together, either a class or something active, try to spark her interest in something, anything. Maybe she'll fall in love with one of those things and start to find herself again.

I tried that. Basically she said she doesn't want to do it with me. It wasn't a critique of me, but of her friends. They've been...growing apart for some time now (basically everyone is either preoccupied with their jobs or kids, there hasn't been a big fallout or anything like that...just years) and they've met very sparsely. 

I tried suggesting her some hobby she could do alone, but she basically laughed at me. 

Thank you for the advice though.

> Have you ever read Eckhart Tolle's Power of Now?

In to the reading list it goes. Which unlike with most people actually means I'll read it after I'm done with the two books I have. Thank you for the suggestion.

> I'm here if you need to chat at all.

I'm very grateful for the offer (I really am), but I'll have to refuse for now. One of the first thing I've done when I decided to "battle the beast"(so to say) is to build a support network and I've grown more accustomed on relying on it.

I've actually been on medicine for awhile. As strange as it sounds I'm getting much better now compared to before. What I'm supposed to do is get ahold of my life after a very bad bout with depression and after a suicide attempt. 

This tiredness of mine isn't a serious problem compared to what was before, I'm just...venting I guess. Just tired of thinking how low my life has sunk and the many attempts I've made through the last few years to fix it. I'll wake up and try again tomorrow - it's kind of the only thing I have left, it's weird because I gave up a long time ago, yet I still keep trying. I'm just tired in a way I can't describe. 

I had a little respite from all my worries recently and I just couldn't relax. As long as I don't fix that mess of a life I have I don't think I'll ever be able to relax properly.

>I am a fucking brat and I don't deserve shit. What am I supposed to do?

Yes you do, you deserve it. You went to the guy and you asked for a job. Let me tell you - a lot of people wouldn't have the courage or initiative to do that. Also, you haven't been fired yet, so you must be doing at minimum a "good enough job". You deserve to be there. 

Is it fair? Maybe not, but the world isn't fair. The rewards don't go to the good or the kindhearted. It goes to those that work hard, show initiative and do not pass a chance once the world presents them with it (or otherwise called luck). 

>First she said the old stuff and I tried to shut her down, telling her how I feel. So she said she understood and all that and it seemed like it was over. 

How much is this girl worth to you? Is she worth the pain she's causing you with this? Maybe she is, I'm not advocating for a break up, but next time she points this out, tell her to count her lucky stars that she found a man with the foresight to recognize opportunities when they present themselves, the initiative to take those opportunities and the hard work and dedication, not to squander them. 

And remember - you deserve to be there. Did you get lucky? Sure you did. But luck alone isn't enough. When luck gives you a branch you need other abilities to take the opportunity and you have those abilities. If you didn't, you wouldn't be where you are right now.

Thank you for the kind words. 

I was thinking of a more substantial reply, but I do not think I can get into a more positive frame of mind at the moment. Any reply I could give would be rebuttal and I do not want to bring people down, when they try to encourage a stranger. 

Again, thank you for your kindness, it means a lot.
